validity.recommendation: Keep row. Note Owner1 = Gazprom covers the offshore string; Turkish onshore string 1 belongs to BOTAS. Endpoint Luleburgaz verified.
validity.researcher_notes: Real, operating, correctly classified (transmission export trunk). Roster: P0765 and P1368 are the two strings, not duplicates: turkstream.info and OIES both state two parallel offshore pipelines, 930 km each, 15.75 bcm/y each (31.5 total). Copied figures 930/813/15.75 are per-string and right. Landfall: first onshore line to Luleburgaz (P0765), second to the Bulgarian border (P1368), matching sheet endpoints. Attribution: offshore owned by Gazprom via South Stream Transport B.V.; onshore string 1 BOTAS; string 2 Gazprom-BOTAS JV (OIES). Diameter 813 = 32 inch exact; sources say 81 cm/810 mm. SegmentCost 7.8 bn USD single weak source (subsea >EUR 7 bn).

fills.researcher_notes: Per-string 15.75 bcm/y confirmed by OIES Insight 65 (two lines, 15.75 bcma each) and by turkstream.info (31.5 bcm total for 2 lines = 2 x 15.75). The 15.75 is a per-string design figure, not a copied system figure. Second source is OIES (independent of operator).

Natural gas line; two independent documents.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Operating. TASS 2026-01-01 (ENTSOG data): 18 bcm to Europe via TurkStream in 2025, record; Newsbase/bne 2025-01-13: TurkStream the only remaining Russian pipeline route to Europe after Ukraine transit ended 2025-01-01. Line-level flow (string 1 Turkey vs string 2 Europe) not split in these sources; system is operating.

cross_row_leads.facts: OIES: the onshore TurkStream string 1 to the Turkish system at Luleburgaz was built/paid by BOTAS; the existing BOTAS line historically carrying Russian gas to the Bulgarian border (Trans-Balkan) was not reused - a new Gazprom-BOTAS JV line was built. Relevant to P2227 duplicate question: P2227 is the old Trans-Balkan Turkish leg, not TurkStream onshore.
